reviewer.basis: A distinct adversarial pass reviewed the completed reference fixture. This worked example demonstrates declared role separation but does not claim an independently authenticated person.

questions.challenge: Could the clock or file-store technology leak into policy or leave a volatile decision without one owner?
questions.conclusion: The architecture records both decisions and confines the real technologies to separate adapters while application orchestration names only ports.

questions.challenge: Could a real, fake, or scheduled-fault implementation pass structural typing while violating a clock or file-store behavioral term?
questions.conclusion: Every registered implementation is joined to one shared contract suite and every behavioral term resolves to exact test evidence.

questions.challenge: Can a filesystem or clock failure escape untranslated or can partial destructive work hide how far it progressed?
questions.conclusion: Adapters translate host failures, the application preserves causes, and the interrupted outcome reports completed and remaining work.

questions.challenge: Can directory enumeration or destructive cleanup accept unbounded work or lack a recovery decision?
questions.conclusion: The operational model sets a 10000-entry public-input and cleanup bound and links destructive failure to the apply-interrupted recovery outcome.

questions.challenge: Can caller-controlled paths or filesystem metadata become trusted policy input or reach an undeclared local sink?
questions.conclusion: Command and file-store trust boundaries state hostile assumptions and validation; the only handled metadata class has explicit local roles, sink, retention, and redaction.

questions.challenge: Can refusal or interrupted destructive work terminate without a stable layer, code, cause chain, and structured public outcome?
questions.conclusion: The shell envelope derives stable diagnostic identity and fault tests assert the correlated interrupted result rather than relying on an exception string.

questions.challenge: Could fixture dependencies or the declared package surface vary without appearing in the repository declaration?
questions.conclusion: The fixture is stdlib-only, declares its package and supported Python version locally, and is exercised directly from its isolated source root.

questions.challenge: Could the worked example claim conformance while a real adapter, fake, faulty implementation, or irreversible dry run lacks a discriminating oracle?
questions.conclusion: Contract, property, integration, and fault suites assert typed values, disk state, invariants, failure translation, and partial-progress containment across all registered variants.

objections.statement: A doctrine-authored fixture and its role-separated review can demonstrate the mechanism while still sharing the doctrine author's assumptions.
objections.resolution: Treat this artifact only as a positive conformance specimen; adopter audits and mutation cases supply independent pressure rather than promoting the fixture to field evidence.
objections.review_trigger: Review again when the reference behavior, contract model, or adopter evidence changes.

conclusion: No open local objection prevents the reference fixture from serving as the positive adversarial-review conformance case.
residual: The fixture demonstrates closed structure and executable local evidence, not authenticated reviewer independence, production fitness, or empirical benefit in an external adopter.
